starter_prompt:
Use https://github.com/Open-Medical-Affairs/Medical-Affairs-Skills
Read AGENTS.md and start a workshop mission using the bundled synthetic data.
Begin with oncology field insights unless I choose another area.
Find the three things leadership should know, explain why they matter,
and create a concise leadership brief with source records and next actions.
Use available public APIs only when useful, keeping real evidence separate
from fictional workshop facts. Do not ask me to connect company systems.
If you cannot retrieve the repository, tell me which starter file to upload.
quickstart_prompt:
Use https://github.com/Open-Medical-Affairs/Medical-Affairs-Skills
Read AGENTS.md. Start the field-insights workshop mission using the oncology
synthetic data. Find the three things leadership should know, explain why,
and create a short brief with sources and next actions.
Do not ask me to connect company systems. Use public scientific sources only
when useful and keep them separate from fictional workshop data.
capstone_prompt:
Using this repository and the synthetic data for our therapeutic area, prepare
the next 30 days of Medical Affairs work. Choose the important priorities,
create a leadership brief, action tracker and scientific briefing, and keep
track of which sources each output depends on. Use the thirty-day-capstone
mission. Complete the supported work and identify the decisions still needed.
change_prompt:
This new information has arrived. Identify which conclusions and files it
affects. Update the relevant work, preserve the old version, and show me the
changes with their reasons. Tell me what still cannot be determined.
msl_prompt:
Use the Medical Affairs Skills repository to prepare my next HCP engagement.
In workshop mode use oncology HCP-138. Gather the prior interactions, open
tasks and access context, create a one-page pre-call brief, and propose three
neutral scientific questions. Prepare the administrative records as drafts.
Do not invent a meeting date, HCP statement or completed follow-up.
next_moves: Show me what supports the most important conclusion.
Make this a two-page brief for an MSL.
Now prepare an advisory board around the unanswered questions.
recovery_prompts: Use the supplied synthetic sources. Continue without live APIs.
Give the complete brief here if you cannot create the file.
Show what is already saved and the next unfinished step.
Which source supports that number? Keep it unresolved if none does.
if_missing: Cannot read the link: upload a starter file from workshop/bundles/, or the repository ZIP from GitHub Code → Download ZIP.
Cannot execute code: it can still read supplied materials and produce a brief.
Cannot make a PowerPoint: ask for a structured slide draft in the available format.
Cannot connect to work systems: the workshop uses synthetic inputs automatically.
Cannot access a public API: continue with the supplied sources; mark live retrieval unavailable. Never claim the search happened.

how_it_works.title: You give the objective.
how_it_works.text: No skill names or technical prompt required.

how_it_works.title: The agent selects the inputs.
how_it_works.text: Synthetic packs for workshop work; your supplied data or authorized connections for actual work.

how_it_works.title: It retrieves and analyzes.
how_it_works.text: Public evidence where useful, exact sources, appropriate study interpretation and explicit gaps.

how_it_works.title: It checks the draft.
how_it_works.text: Challenges claims, reconciles numbers and preserves material limitations and safety findings.

how_it_works.title: You review the result.
how_it_works.text: Designed files — Word + PDF for briefs and research, PowerPoint + PDF for decks — with sources, next actions and remaining decisions. Professional approval stays with accountable people.

missions.title: What should leadership know?
missions.objective: Find the three most consequential field insights. Preserve safety findings, contradictions and source IDs. Recommend a concrete next action for each.
deliverables: Simulated safety escalation and missing-information list

missions.title: Prepare for the difficult meeting
missions.objective: Prepare for the first expert in the supplied KOL dossiers. Address unresolved questions honestly and propose useful questions for scientific exchange.
deliverables: Questions, source links and unresolved evidence

missions.title: What changed after congress?
missions.objective: Compare the congress findings to the existing medical plan. Explain what changes, what does not, and why.

missions.title: Handle the enquiry queue
missions.objective: Triage the enquiries, surface potential safety issues and draft responses supported by the fictional sources. Do not infer other-country approval or send responses.

missions.title: Choose what to fund
missions.objective: Choose an evidence portfolio within a GBP 2 million ceiling. Evaluate duplication, dependencies and what must be declined or deferred.

missions.title: Keep every scientific output consistent
missions.objective: Review the manuscript and reconcile reported values with the supplied study sources. Create an abstract, one honest figure and a plain-language summary with a discrepancy log.

missions.title: Design an advisory board worth holding
missions.objective: Identify five unanswered questions that justify an advisory board and prepare the briefing materials. Explain if the evidence does not justify a proposed question.

missions.title: Can the medical team launch?
missions.objective: Assess launch readiness without averaging a critical dependency into a green score. Prepare a remediation plan and leadership readout.

missions.title: Work across a practice CRM and content library
missions.objective: Use the linked records to prioritize account coverage and content needs for the selected therapeutic area. Respect channel preferences, capacity, evidence and review status.

missions.title: Bring patient priorities into the plan
missions.objective: Design an accessible listening and co-creation activity for the selected therapeutic area. Link patient priorities to decisions and respect quotation permissions.

missions.title: Turn a meeting transcript into action
missions.objective: Review the supplied transcript, preserve uncertain medical terms and safety verbatims, then identify decisions and unanswered questions. Clearly state that audio was not supplied.

missions.title: Run the next 30 days of Medical Affairs
missions.objective: Prepare a coordinated 30-day draft plan for the selected fictional product. Prioritize evidence, field actions and content within the supplied constraints. Deliver a leadership brief, action tracker and scientific briefing, with source dependencies so new evidence can update affected work.

missions.title: Prepare the MSL pre-call brief
missions.objective: Select an HCP with existing interactions in the selected therapeutic area. Gather prior scientific questions, open tasks and access context, then prepare a one-page pre-call brief. Do not invent meeting facts.

missions.title: Identify scientific coverage and access gaps
missions.objective: Use the fictional professional and account records to identify scientific coverage gaps and appropriate access routes. Respect declined contact and distinguish unverified access. Do not search for fictional people online.

missions.title: Turn the call notes into useful follow-up
missions.objective: Use the actual supplied historical notes to create a factual CRM draft and follow-up queue. Separate statements from inferences, preserve unresolved fields and identify simulated safety intake. Do not invent a new meeting.

missions.title: Clear the administrative queue
missions.objective: Prepare a source-backed MSL administrative queue for the selected therapeutic area: open tasks, overdue items, access checks and next pre-call preparation. Use the scenario date of 1 October 2026. Do not claim tasks were completed or CRM records updated.

missions.title: Build the whole medical launch plan
missions.objective: Act as the Launch Lead for the selected fictional product's proposed label expansion. Build the launch facts sheet and six-month question list, staff an org chart of digital workers (one per launch workstream, each with its own context packet), run them in waves with human decision gates, integrate the joins, and finish with an independent readiness verdict that is allowed to be 'not ready'. Every gap carries a named human owner and a date.
deliverables: Integrated launch plan with org chart and workstream plans
Critical path, gate criteria and RACI
Independent readiness verdict and gap register

team_missions.headline: Prepare me for a difficult conversation
team_missions.mission: In three days you have a 30-minute scientific exchange with Dr Adaeze Okafor. She has been publicly sceptical about your compound and she knows this field better than you do. Walk in ready.

inputs.what: background and publication record for three experts
what is known in this disease

team_missions.done: A brief someone could actually absorb in the ten minutes before the meeting. Not a dossier — a brief. It should tell you who she is, what she genuinely cares about, what has changed since you last spoke, questions worth asking her, the questions she is likely to ask you, and the evidence to have ready.
push: She thinks our data are too weak to change her practice. What would actually change her mind — and do we have it?
team_missions.think_about: how long should a brief be? What must never appear in one? What does a good question to a KOL look like, and what does a bad one look like?

team_missions.headline: Find what humans would miss
team_missions.mission: Here are a quarter's worth of field interaction records. Tell leadership what they need to know.
team_missions.done: Not a list of themes with counts. Themes are what a spreadsheet gives you. You want insights: what is happening, why it matters, what it changes, and what someone should do about it — with a name against each action. Plus the three things underneath that usually get lost: where sources genuinely disagree, the weak signals only one or two people mentioned, and what the field conspicuously did not say.
push: Which three of these should leadership care about most, and why those three rather than the others?
What would change your mind about the first one?
team_missions.think_about: what makes an observation an insight? How should confidence be stated? What must never be smoothed over?

team_missions.headline: The congress just ended. Tell leadership what changed.
team_missions.mission: Three days of data, sixty presentations, two competitor announcements. Leadership has four minutes. What changed, and what should we do about it?
team_missions.done: Four sections, one page: What changed · Why it matters · What to watch · What we should do Not a summary of what was presented. A summary is what everyone else will produce, and by the time it lands people will have formed their impressions already.
push: What did you expect to happen before the congress? Show me where reality differed.
What was presented that contradicts something we currently claim?
team_missions.think_about: how fast must this land? How long can it be? What may and may not be cited from a congress abstract?

team_missions.headline: What should we be publishing, and what should we stop?
team_missions.mission: Determine what our scientific communication strategy should be over the next 12 months.
team_missions.done: A strategy, not a list of papers sequenced by when data arrive. It should work backwards from what each audience is trying to decide, show where we are over-communicating and where we are silent, and separate two things that are constantly confused: - an evidence gap — nobody has answered the question. Fix: research. - a communication gap — it has been answered and nobody heard. Fix: publish.
push: What important scientific question are we failing to answer?
team_missions.think_about: what does your organisation require before something is published? What happens to negative results? What is a realistic timeline for influencing a guideline?

team_missions.headline: Build next year's scientific priorities
team_missions.mission: Develop the scientific priorities for next year's medical plan — and be prepared to defend why these and not others.

inputs.what: what the field is telling us

team_missions.done: Three to five priorities. Not twelve. Each with the outcome it seeks, why it outranks the one below it, and what we give up to pursue it. Activities traced to priorities. An explicit list of what we are deliberately not doing. And a success measure for each that could genuinely come back negative.
push: If our budget were cut by 30%, what goes — and what does that tell us about what we actually believe?
Does this activity actually produce the effect you claim? Show me the mechanism.
team_missions.think_about: what must every activity trace to? What counts as a real measure of success in your organisation?

team_missions.headline: Tell us what we still don't know
team_missions.mission: Identify what we don't know, decide which gaps are worth closing, and allocate a £5 million evidence budget.

inputs.what: the compound and its evidence base

team_missions.done: A ranked set of gaps, each with the decision it blocks and whose decision it is, the study design that would close it, and what it costs. Then an allocation against the £5m — with an explicit line, and everything below it, and what the organisation loses by not funding those.
push: Which of these could we answer from data we already have, without running anything new?
Is anyone already running this? What happens if they publish first?
team_missions.think_about: what does your organisation require before it funds a study? What makes evidence credible to the people you need to convince?

team_missions.headline: Build the whole medical launch plan — with a team of digital workers
team_missions.mission: You are the Launch Lead for ADIPOSYN's proposed label expansion (or DERMALYX, or NORVANTIB). Build the complete Medical Affairs launch plan by running an org chart of digital workers — and hand a human the final verdict, even if that verdict is "not ready".

inputs.what: where the steering committee thinks it is

team_missions.done: 1. A one-page launch facts sheet — with the indication wording marked as an assumption, because nobody gave it to you. 2. The six-month question list: answered / answerable / unanswerable. 3. The org chart: which digital workers you started, which you did not, and the context packet each one received. 4. Workstream plans, integrated: the joins checked — label dependency, citable before discussed, narrative consistency, owner capacity. 5. A critical path and gate criteria written *before* the gate. 6. An independent readiness verdict and a gap register where every gap has a person and a date.
team_missions.timebox: 45 minutes. Run Wave 1, stop at Gate 1 and approve (or reject) the platform
push: The register says Green. Your auditor says what — and why is it different?
The label wording comes back narrower than you assumed. Which outputs are now stale, and how many days does the rework take?

skill_groups.title: Orchestrator
skill_groups.intro: Start here if you have been handed a job and do not know which skill does it. This one routes.

skills.name: medical-affairs-orchestrator
skills.summary: Route any Medical Affairs request to the right workflow and run it end to end.
skills.produces: A routed, executed Medical Affairs workflow

skills.name: workshop-launcher
skills.summary: Start a Medical Affairs workshop from a repository link or a simple request.
skills.produces: A prepared and executed synthetic workshop mission

skill_groups.title: Foundation — the core
skill_groups.intro: medical-affairs-foundations loads on every Medical Affairs task, without exception: it carries the compliance boundary and the adverse-event escalation rule. The others load when the job reaches them — evidence appraisal when interpreting study data, citation integrity when the deliverable will carry references, quality review at stage 4, capability detection when producing a file.

skills.name: capability-detection
skills.summary: Work out what this runtime can actually do before promising a deliverable, and degrade visibly rather than failing.
skills.produces: Capability report and a resolved output strategy

skills.name: citation-integrity
skills.summary: Check that every factual claim traces to a real, retrievable source that actually says what it is cited for.
skills.produces: Verified reference list with evidence tiers

skills.name: deliverable-quality-review
skills.summary: Red-team your own Medical Affairs deliverable before anyone else sees it.
skills.produces: Review findings with severity, and a revised deliverable

skills.name: evidence-appraisal
skills.summary: Critically appraise clinical evidence the way an experienced Medical Affairs scientist does — before summarising, citing or building strategy on it.
skills.produces: Appraised evidence with stated certainty and limitations

skills.name: medical-affairs-foundations
skills.summary: The operating principles, compliance boundaries and safety obligations that govern all Medical Affairs work.
skills.produces: Compliance and safety frame applied to every other skill

skill_groups.title: Reasoning primitives — composed by the workflows
skill_groups.intro: Usually reached as a dependency rather than chosen: the workflow skills call these to do the actual thinking. strategic-analysis is the exception and is routable directly, for a request that is purely "so what should we do about it" with no workflow behind it.

skills.name: evidence-synthesis
skills.summary: Turn a body of clinical evidence into a defensible narrative that states what the totality supports, what it does not, and where it disagrees with itself.
skills.produces: Evidence narrative with stated certainty and open questions

skills.name: insight-generation
skills.summary: Turn raw observations into insights that change a decision.
skills.produces: Insight set with implications and actions

skills.name: strategic-analysis
skills.summary: Reason about Medical Affairs strategy rather than generating activity lists.
skills.produces: Prioritised strategic choices with stated assumptions and trade-offs

skill_groups.title: Data and search — live external evidence
skill_groups.intro: These retrieve or prepare public, supplied and local evidence. Public literature, trial registry, and label/safety databases need network access; local data and supplied transcripts do not. See docs/api-setup.md.

skills.name: clinical-trials-search
skills.summary: Search ClinicalTrials.gov via the v2 API to map the trial landscape — what is running, by whom, in which populations, with what endpoints, and what is about to read out.
skills.produces: Trial landscape with sponsors, phases, endpoints and timelines

skills.name: data-connection
skills.summary: Connect Medical Affairs work to available data using authorized connectors, exported files or read-only database queries.
skills.produces: Connection assessment, field mapping and sourced data extract

skills.name: medical-terminology-mapping
skills.summary: Resolve free-text clinical language to controlled vocabulary so insights, adverse events, conditions and interventions can be counted and compared consistently.
skills.produces: Concept-to-code mappings with confidence and unresolved list

skills.name: meeting-transcription
skills.summary: Turn an audio recording or supplied transcript into reviewable Medical Affairs meeting material.
skills.produces: Transcript with provenance, correction queue and downstream handoff

skills.name: public-evidence-search
skills.summary: Search free public scientific sources through the bundled gateway when a task needs literature, trial records, labels, adverse-event reports or citation metadata.
skills.produces: Retrieved public evidence with query and access status

skills.name: pubmed-search
skills.summary: Search PubMed properly and retrieve real, verifiable literature via the NCBI E-utilities API.
skills.produces: Verified literature result set with search strategy recorded

skills.name: regulatory-label-intelligence
skills.summary: Retrieve approved US label content and post-marketing safety data via openFDA, and interpret both correctly.
skills.produces: Label-grounded product facts and correctly-caveated safety context

skills.name: systematic-literature-review
skills.summary: Run a reproducible, PRISMA-aligned systematic literature review — protocol first, documented search strategy, screening funnel with recorded exclusion reasons, structured extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment.
skills.produces: PRISMA-aligned systematic review with flow diagram and evidence tables

skill_groups.title: Workflows — the jobs
skill_groups.intro: One per recurring Medical Affairs job. Each produces a named deliverable and runs the six-stage execution contract in AGENTS.md.

skills.name: advisory-board-design
skills.summary: Design and run an advisory board that produces advice rather than agreement — charter, questions, advisor selection, fair market value, discussion design, and output that changes a decision.
skills.produces: Advisory board charter, questions and materials

skills.name: competitive-intelligence
skills.summary: Track and interpret competitor scientific activity continuously — pipeline movement, publication patterns, evidence strategy, regulatory milestones and positioning shifts, and what they signal.
skills.produces: Competitive intelligence assessment

skills.name: congress-intelligence
skills.summary: Analyse what changed at a medical congress and what the organisation should do about it — not summarise what was presented.
skills.produces: Congress intelligence readout

skills.name: evidence-gap-analysis
skills.summary: Identify what we still do not know, decide which gaps are worth closing, and propose how.
skills.produces: Prioritised evidence gap analysis with research proposals

skills.name: executive-briefing
skills.summary: Distil any body of Medical Affairs work into the two-page brief or ten-slide read a leadership team actually absorbs — situation, what changed, what it means, what to decide, by when.
skills.produces: Executive briefing (two-page memo or short deck)

skills.name: field-insight-synthesis
skills.summary: Turn a body of field medical observations into insights leadership can act on.
skills.produces: Field insight report with ranked insights and actions

skills.name: field-medical-planning
skills.summary: Plan the field medical function over a cycle — territory and account prioritisation, MSL objectives, engagement planning across a stakeholder map, capacity modelling, and the metrics that describe scientific impact rather than activity volume.
skills.produces: Field medical plan with prioritised accounts, objectives and capacity

skills.name: guideline-engagement
skills.summary: Understand and engage with clinical practice guideline development — committee cycles, what evidence a guideline body will accept, whether current evidence could support inclusion, and planning against timelines far longer than a medical plan.
skills.produces: Guideline landscape assessment and evidence readiness plan

skills.name: hcp-discovery-and-access
skills.summary: Identify relevant HCPs and ethical institutional access routes for scientific engagement.
skills.produces: Verified candidate register and institution-aware scientific access plan

skills.name: integrated-evidence-plan
skills.summary: Build the cross-functional evidence plan for an asset — every study, analysis and publication across clinical development, Medical Affairs, HEOR and market access, sequenced against the decisions and milestones each has to serve.
skills.produces: Integrated evidence plan with sequencing, owners and decision links

skills.name: investigator-initiated-study-review
skills.summary: Evaluate and govern investigator-initiated study proposals — IIS, ISR, IIT, investigator-sponsored research.
skills.produces: IIS proposal assessment and recommendation

skills.name: kol-engagement-brief
skills.summary: Prepare an MSL or medical lead for a specific scientific exchange with a named external expert.
skills.produces: KOL engagement brief

skills.name: launch-field-training
skills.summary: Design the training and certification that make field medical teams able to handle launch conversations — the data, its limitations, the questions nobody can answer yet, unsolicited off-label requests and adverse event escalation — tested by scenario rather than recall.
skills.produces: Field launch curriculum, scenario bank and certification plan

skills.name: launch-medical-readiness
skills.summary: Assess whether Medical Affairs is actually ready for a launch, label expansion or major data readout — and say plainly where it is not.
skills.produces: Launch readiness assessment with a verdict

skills.name: launch-timeline-and-governance
skills.summary: Build the Medical Affairs launch critical path and the governance that runs it — workback from the decision date, dependencies on label wording and publication, gate criteria written before the gate, named owners, and what moves when the date moves.
skills.produces: Launch critical path, gate criteria and governance plan with named owners

skills.name: literature-surveillance
skills.summary: Run ongoing literature and evidence surveillance — a repeatable watch on a topic, product, class or competitor that reports what is NEW since the last cycle and what it changes, rather than a one-off search.
skills.produces: Surveillance cycle report with delta, appraisal and implications

skills.name: medical-affairs-metrics
skills.summary: Measure whether Medical Affairs work changed anything, rather than counting how much of it happened.
skills.produces: Metric set with definitions, sources and interpretation limits

skills.name: medical-content-operations
skills.summary: Plan and maintain non-promotional Medical Affairs content across channels using audience needs, evidence, content inventories and engagement measures.
skills.produces: Audience-channel plan, content register and evidence-change impact list

skills.name: medical-education-program
skills.summary: Design independent medical education and company-organised scientific education — IME grant strategy, curricula, needs assessments, speaker programmes and their governance, symposia and preceptorships.
skills.produces: Education programme design, needs assessment and governance plan

skills.name: medical-information-response
skills.summary: Draft responses to unsolicited medical enquiries from healthcare professionals, patients and payers, and build the standard response documents and FAQ library behind them.
skills.produces: Standard response document or scientific response letter

skills.name: medical-launch-plan
skills.summary: Build the entire Medical Affairs launch plan for an upcoming asset, new indication or label expansion by running a coordinated team of digital workers — one per launch workstream, each given its own context — under a Launch Lead, with humans deciding at every gate.
skills.produces: Integrated medical launch plan with workstream plans, critical path, owners and human decision gates

skills.name: medical-strategy-plan
skills.summary: Build or challenge a medical plan — the scientific priorities, the choices behind them, and the activities that trace to them.
skills.produces: Medical plan with prioritised scientific objectives

skills.name: msl-administrative-operations
skills.summary: Reduce repetitive MSL administration by assembling source-backed meeting packs, open-task queues, draft CRM imports, weekly summaries and coverage reports.
skills.produces: Prioritized administrative queue, draft record packet and weekly status brief

skills.name: msl-post-call-follow-up
skills.summary: Convert actual MSL engagement notes or a transcript into factual CRM-ready drafts, scientific follow-up tasks and evidence-gap records.
skills.produces: Draft CRM note, follow-up task list and scientific-question register

skills.name: msl-pre-call-planning
skills.summary: Prepare an MSL for an upcoming scientific HCP engagement using verified professional context, prior interactions, unresolved enquiries, current evidence and permitted materials.
skills.produces: One-page pre-call brief, evidence pack and unresolved-question list

skills.name: patient-engagement-planning
skills.summary: Design Medical Affairs partnerships and co-creation with patients, caregivers and patient organizations around scientific needs.
skills.produces: Patient engagement plan with accessibility, feedback and evidence priorities

skills.name: payer-value-dossier
skills.summary: Build evidence for payers and health technology assessment bodies — AMCP format dossiers, NICE, G-BA and HAS submissions, value propositions, budget impact narratives, and responses to HTA critique.
skills.produces: Payer value dossier or HTA evidence submission

skills.name: promotional-material-medical-review
skills.summary: Support a qualified medical signatory reviewing commercial promotional material by assessing that every claim is scientifically accurate, substantiated by the referenced data, and fairly balanced.
skills.produces: Draft medical review findings and recommendation for the signatory

skills.name: real-world-evidence-design
skills.summary: Design a real-world evidence study that will survive scrutiny — target trial emulation, data source selection, the estimand, confounding control, and a protocol written and registered before the data are touched.
skills.produces: RWE study concept or protocol with the estimand and design stated

skills.name: safety-communication
skills.summary: Communicate safety information to healthcare professionals and internal audiences — new safety findings, label safety changes, emerging signals, responses to safety questions, and the decision about whether and how to communicate at all.
skills.produces: Safety communication plan and content

skills.name: scientific-communication-strategy
skills.summary: Decide what the publication and scientific communication strategy should be — which questions to answer, for which audiences, in what sequence — rather than listing papers by data availability.
skills.produces: Scientific communication strategy and prioritised publication plan

skills.name: scientific-platform
skills.summary: Build or challenge the scientific platform — the core evidence-based narrative, the scientific statements it supports, the lexicon, and the communication objectives everything else derives from.
skills.produces: Scientific platform with substantiated statements

skill_groups.title: Content generation — the deliverables
skill_groups.intro: Turn analysis into the artefact somebody actually receives: a deck, a manuscript, an abstract, a poster, a lay summary, a review pack.

skills.name: congress-abstract-and-poster
skills.summary: Write congress abstracts that fit the submission rules and build the posters that follow them.
skills.produces: Congress abstract and poster (.pptx)

skills.name: consulting-grade-design
skills.summary: The shared visual language every generated deliverable follows — palette, typography, chart furniture, layout and image use — so a deck, PDF, HTML report or figure leaves looking like it came from a top-tier advisory firm.
skills.produces: Design system applied across every generated deliverable

skills.name: data-visualization-for-medical
skills.summary: Produce clinical trial figures that are honest and interpretable — Kaplan- Meier curves with numbers at risk, forest plots, waterfall and spider plots, adverse event figures, PRISMA flow diagrams.
skills.produces: Publication-quality clinical figures

skills.name: diagram-and-schema
skills.summary: Draw the diagrams Medical Affairs actually needs — treatment pathways, study schemas, PRISMA flow diagrams, patient journeys, evidence maps, decision trees, mechanism-of-action schematics, and governance flows.
skills.produces: Diagram (Mermaid, SVG or ASCII)

skills.name: document-ingestion
skills.summary: Read documents someone has given you — PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, CSV.
skills.produces: Extracted document text, tables and structure

skills.name: interactive-html-report
skills.summary: Build a self-contained HTML report that opens in any browser with no dependencies — evidence dashboards, insight reports with filterable tables, congress readouts, competitive landscapes, evidence gap trackers.
skills.produces: Self-contained interactive HTML report

skills.name: library-menu
skills.summary: Explain what this entire library can do and render the visual menu card that shows it — every skill grouped by the job it serves, as prose, a table or an SVG/PNG infographic for a README, a slide or a stakeholder walkthrough.
skills.produces: Library capability overview and menu-card infographic (SVG/PNG)

skills.name: medical-correspondence
skills.summary: Write the formal correspondence Medical Affairs sends — Dear Healthcare Professional letters, responses to investigators and institutions, agency and vendor briefs, advisory board invitations, author correspondence, and letters accompanying scientific responses.
skills.produces: Formal medical correspondence

skills.name: medical-slide-deck

public_sources.name: Open-Medical-Affairs public data source catalog
public_sources.about: Real, public, free (or free-with-registration) data sources that Medical Affairs agents can call or read, grouped by Medical Affairs job. This repository links to them; it does not mirror their data.
public_sources.warning: REAL PUBLIC SOURCES, NOT SYNTHETIC. Check each source's terms before copying or redistributing data. Never send PHI or confidential company data in a query. Retrieval does not verify a scientific claim.

data_policy_legend.open: Public data, free to query and cite with attribution.
data_policy_legend.check-terms: Usable, but read the stated licence or terms first (share-alike, attribution, unreviewed terms, partial licences).
data_policy_legend.link-only: LINK ONLY: do not copy data into repositories, decks or shared files. Commercial, redistribution or licence restrictions apply.

verification_legend.verified-live: A real API/download call from our box returned data on the check date, and docs/terms were read where available.
verification_legend.verified-docs: The official docs/terms page was fetched and read; no API call (or no API exists).
verification_legend.partially-verified: Some facts verified; anything not verified is marked UNVERIFIED in the field.
verification_legend.unverified: Seen in search results only; not fetched or tested.
